# Scythe simulations

<!-- GENERATED by tools/config_reference.jl from src/config.jl and src/run_driver.jl.
     Do not edit by hand: change the code (docstrings, defaults, registries) and run
     `julia --project=. tools/config_reference.jl`. -->

Each directory here is one case: a `scythe_config.toml` (what is run), a launcher
`run.jl`, SLURM launchers `*.sbatch`, a `README.md` for the case, and optionally an
`examples/` directory of alternate grids. A run is ONE config file: the example files are
copied into `scythe_config.toml` by hand, never layered on the command line, so the
resolved `scythe_config.toml` written into the run root is the whole record. The
configuration describes WHAT is run, never how: workers, threads and the scheduler are
launcher flags, recorded for provenance in `segments.csv` but never in the config, so two
runs that differ only in launcher produce identical output.

## Cases

- [`ocean_2D_rce/`](ocean_2D_rce/README.md) — `ocean_2D_rce/scythe_config.toml`
- [`ocean_warm_bubble/`](ocean_warm_bubble/README.md) — `ocean_warm_bubble/scythe_config.toml`
- [`tc_axisym/`](tc_axisym/README.md) — `tc_axisym/scythe_config.toml`

## Launching

A `run.jl` is `using Scythe` plus the launcher call and nothing else, so it runs from any
directory under any Julia environment where Scythe is installed (`<env>` below; a Scythe
checkout itself works, `--project=/path/to/Scythe.jl`). Radiation (RRTMGP) is part of
Scythe and needs no special environment. To run a case outside the repository, copy its
`scythe_config.toml` and `run.jl` to a directory and run it there.

### Local: `run.jl`

```
julia --project=<env> run.jl [--config scythe_config.toml] [--set key.path=value ...]
      [--resume] [--workers N | --workers-per-patch a,b,c] [--worker-threads N]
      [--blas-threads N] [--slurm]
```

| flag | meaning |
|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | the run's one config file (default: `scythe_config.toml` beside `run.jl`); a positional argument is refused |
| `--set key.path=value` | run control: `output.dir`, `run.integration_time`, ... (repeatable, applied in order; recorded in the resolved config's header) |
| `--resume` | continue the run in `output.dir` from its `segments.csv` |
| `--workers N` | N workers on a single-patch run |
| `--workers-per-patch a,b,c` | worker group size per nest patch (one entry per patch) |
| `--worker-threads N` | Julia threads per worker (0 = split the machine) |
| `--blas-threads N` | OpenBLAS threads per process (default 1; 0 = OpenBLAS default) |
| `--slurm` | add the workers with `ClusterManagers.addprocs_slurm` (inside an allocation) |
| `--segment k` | internal: the orchestrator's per-segment child |

Before anything is written (fresh start or `--resume`), `run_simulation` runs
`preflight_checks`: Springsteel new enough, the config validates, and, when
`physics.radiation.scheme = "rrtmgp"`, the RRTMGP lookup tables already local (run
`tools/rrtmgp_prewarm.jl` once on a login node; compute nodes have no network). A fresh
start refuses an `output.dir` that already holds a run (model output is experimental
data: `mv` the tree aside, never `rm` it). `--resume` re-reads
`<output.dir>/scythe_config.toml` and runs the segments not recorded `done`; the only `--set` it
accepts is `run.integration_time` (to extend a run); give the tree to resume with
`--set output.dir=...`, which the launchers use only to locate it.

### Cluster: `*.sbatch`

```
sbatch simulations/<case>/<launcher>.sbatch [--set key.path=value ...] [--resume]
```

The sbatch scripts run `julia --project=${SCYTHE_PROJECT:-$SCYTHE}
$SCYTHE/simulations/<case>/run.jl ...`, where `SCYTHE` (from `SCYTHE_DIR`) is the checkout
or run directory holding `simulations/<case>/scythe_config.toml` and `SCYTHE_PROJECT` is
any environment where Scythe is installed. They set the node shape and
`JULIA_NUM_THREADS`, give a fresh job its own `output.dir` unless one is `--set` (TC),
tee everything to `<output.dir>/job_stdout.log`, and pass every argument through to
`run.jl`. Environment variables no longer configure a run.

## The config file and `--set`

- The case file is read, then each `--set` applies in order. Keys absent from the file
  take the struct defaults below, so a case file lists only what it needs. `--set` is
  for run control (where the output goes, how long to run); a physics or grid change
  belongs in the config file, so that the file IS the record.
- `--set` values are parsed as TOML (`TOML.parse("v = " * rhs)`) and fall back to a bare
  string: `--set physics.boundary_layer.scheme=louis`, `--set timestep.ts=0.25`,
  `--set grid.num_cells=[15,15,15]`, `--set physics.boundary_layer.K_max=inf`,
  `--set 'output.formats=["netcdf","csv"]'` all work.
- Unknown keys anywhere are errors naming the section; enum values are checked against
  the sets below; `inf` round-trips.
- Paths (`output.dir`, `reference_state.sounding`, `initial_conditions.file.paths`)
  resolve against the directory of the file that set them; `--set` paths against the
  working directory; `@scythe/` is the package root. The written config holds absolute
  paths.
- Implied values are resolved at build: `physics.microphysics.rain_moments = 0` (2 under
  ice, else 1), `physics.radiation.z_max = 0` (= `physics.sponge.z_damp`),
  `timestep.ts_per_patch = []` (every patch at `ts`), `numerics.cfl_interval = 0`
  (= `output.interval`).
- Cross-section rules (ice with Louis, `exact_si` with `state_dependent_si`, Smagorinsky
  on XZ, periodic cylindrical grids, segments without checkpoints, ...) are checked by
  `validate(cfg)` at build.

## Output layout

Always the segmented layout, even for one segment, so readers handle one shape:

```
<output.dir>/scythe_config.toml       resolved config (every field) + provenance header
<output.dir>/reference.ref            reference column: z p rho_d rho_v rho_c
<output.dir>/ics.csv | nest{i}_ics.csv  initial conditions
<output.dir>/segments.csv             one row per segment (columns below)
<output.dir>/boundary_conditions.toml the BC every variable actually has, per patch (see below)
<output.dir>/job_stdout.log           (sbatch launchers only)
<output.dir>/seg_NN/scythe_config.toml  the same config; the segment's values in the header
<output.dir>/seg_NN/segment_stdout.log
<output.dir>/seg_NN/[nest{i}/]<t>.nc | <t>.jld2 | scythe_{out,err}.log
```

`<t>` is LOCAL to the segment: each segment starts at t = 0 from the previous segment's
final checkpoint and writes its own t = 0 snapshot (a duplicate of the previous
segment's last one). Absolute time is `t_offset_s + t`. The radiation clock is carried:
each segment runs with `start_hour = physics.radiation.start_hour + t_offset_s / 3600`.

`segments.csv` columns:

- `segment`
- `dir`
- `t_offset_s`
- `integration_time_s`
- `ts`
- `output_interval_s`
- `restart_file`
- `status`
- `scythe_sha`
- `started`
- `finished`
- `n_patches`
- `ts_actual`
- `start_hour`
- `workers`
- `threads`
- `host`
- `note`

## Configuration reference

Tables in the order `write_config` writes them. Only the ACTIVE
`[initial_conditions.<method>]` table is written back to an output `scythe_config.toml`;
all four are held so a `--set` can switch `method`.

### `[run]`

what is being run and for how long.

| key | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `"scythe_run"` | run label, used in log lines and output naming. |
| `equation_set` | string | `"moist_compressible_XZ"` | canonical Scythe equation set, a key of `EQUATION_SETS`. |
| `integration_time` | float | `432000.0` | total simulated time [s]. |
| `segment_length` | float | `0.0` | restart granularity [s]; each segment is one process; 0 = one segment. |

### `[output]`

where and how often the run writes.

| key | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | string | `"output"` | output root; relative to the file that set it; absolute in the struct. |
| `interval` | float | `3600.0` | analysis-output cadence [s]. |
| `restart_interval` | float | `21600.0` | JLD2 checkpoint cadence [s]; must be > 0 when `run.segment_length > 0`. |
| `formats` | [string] | `["netcdf"]` | analysis formats, from `OUTPUT_FORMAT_SYMBOLS` (`netcdf`, `csv`, `netcdf_raw`). |
| `sidecars` | bool | `false` | also write the per-tile MYNN and radiation NetCDF sidecars. |
| `netcdf_grid` | string (enum) | `"regular"` | grid the NetCDF output is written on (`regular`). |
| `netcdf_derivatives` | bool | `false` | `netcdf_raw` also writes derivative slots. |

### `[grid]`

the patches and the vertical axis.

| key | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `geometry` | string | `"RiRk"` | Springsteel geometry name (`RiRk`, `RZ`, `RLR`, `RRR`); must suit `run.equation_set`. |
| `boundaries` | [float] | `[0.0, 300000.0]` | patch edges [m], outermost last; length 2 = single patch. |
| `num_cells` | [int] | `[50]` | horizontal B-spline cells per patch; length `length(boundaries) - 1`. |
| `z_top` | float | `25000.0` | model lid [m]. |
| `num_cells_k` | int | `50` | vertical B-spline cells. |

### `[boundary_conditions]`

the boundary condition of every prognostic variable, set by four family rules plus per-variable overrides. The resolved per-variable table is written to `<output.dir>/boundary_conditions.toml` and printed at startup.

| key | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lateral` | string (enum) | `"periodic"` | `walls` or `periodic` (XZ only). XZ walls: every variable Neumann (zero gradient) on both sides, except `u` and `w` Dirichlet (zero). Cylindrical sets (always walls): axis = Neumann except `u`, `v` Dirichlet; outer wall = Neumann except `u` Dirichlet (`v` and `w` are Neumann there). periodic: `PeriodicBC` on every variable. Nest interfaces are set by the nesting, not here. |
| `vertical_scalars` | string (enum) | `"natural"` | GROUND BC of every variable except `w` (always Dirichlet zero) and the sedimenting slots (always natural at the ground): `d2` second derivative zero, `natural` unconstrained, `neumann` zero gradient, `r1t1x` = `d2` except `rho_d`, `rho_t`, `E_t`, `Q_ss` Neumann and `p` the rigid-wall pressure condition (`dp'/dz = -g rho_t'` installed before every fit). Natural by default: a surface layer is logarithmic, and `d2` forces the velocity and scalar gradients constant there. The whole family must share one condition (freeing `p` or `rho_t` alone blows up); with all of it natural the resting-column SI ceiling is 0.875-0.9375 s (0.9375-1.0 s under `d2`) and the 12 h no-physics TC hold is indistinguishable from `d2` (1.78% vs 1.73% of the deficit filled). Never `neumann`: on `p` at the ground it drains the pressure field. |
| `vertical_scalars_lid` | string (enum) | `"natural"` | LID BC of the same family (every variable except `w`, always Dirichlet zero), same values as `vertical_scalars`. Natural by default: `d2` at a rigid lid over-constrains the perturbation fields and drifts warm over days (multi-day 2D RCE: lid T anomaly 0.5 K at 48 h, crash at 277 h; restarted with a natural lid the anomaly decays). Clean at ts = 0.75 s on the RCE case; ts = 1.0 s showed a transient adjustment that `d2` did not. |
| `sedimentation_lid` | string (enum) | `"natural"` | lid BC of the sedimenting slots (rain, two-moment rain number, the twelve ice slots): `natural` (unconstrained) or `wall` (left on `vertical_scalars_lid`). Only the slot VALUES: on a B-spline vertical every sedimentation FLUX is fitted with a zero-flux lid either way, so no hydrometeor enters through the top. |
| `override` | table | `{}` | expert per-variable overrides applied after the family rules: `{<variable> = {<side> = <bc>}}` with side `inner`/`outer`/`bottom`/`top` and bc `natural`, `dirichlet`, `neumann`, `second_derivative`, `periodic` or `r1t1x`; `inner`/`outer` act on the domain's own edges (a nest interface is always the nesting's), refused under periodic. |

### `[timestep]`

the time step of every patch.

| key | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ts` | float | `0.5` | root (coarsest) patch time step [s]. |
| `ts_per_patch` | [float] | `[]` | per-patch steps [s]; empty = every patch at `ts`. |
| `scale` | float | `1.0` | multiplies `ts` and every `ts_per_patch` entry. |

| `exact` | bool | `true` | pre-balance the reference state on the model grid (`:exact_reference_state`). |
| `consistent_qss` | bool | `true` | reference `Q_ss` consistent with the discrete retrieval (`:consistent_qss_reference`). |
| `hydrostatic` | bool | `true` | discretely hydrostatic reference (`:hydrostatic_reference`). |

| `K` | float | `0.0` | constant momentum viscosity [m²/s] (`constant` only). |
| `heat` | bool | `true` | also mix entropy/heat with K/Pr_t. |
| `water` | bool | `false` | also mix every water species with K/Sc_t: total water, vapor, cloud, rain (+ number) and, with ice, every ice mass and moment, all with the one K (NOT energy consistent). |
| `Pr_t` | float | `1.0` | turbulent Prandtl number. |
| `Sc_t` | float | `1.0` | turbulent Schmidt number. |

| `cfl_interval` | float | `0.0` | CFL report cadence [s]; 0 = `output.interval`, resolved at build. |

## Boundary conditions

Every prognostic variable has a boundary condition on each of its four sides: `inner` and
`outer` (the axis and the outer wall on the cylindrical sets; left and right on XZ), and
`bottom` (the ground) and `top` (the lid). They are NOT listed one by one in the config:
`[boundary_conditions]` holds four family rules that `build_boundary_conditions`
(src/config_build.jl) applies to the run's variable list, then the per-variable
`override` entries, then `build_nest` sets the nest interfaces. What each family value
does, exactly:

| key = value | rule applied |
|---|---|
| `lateral = "walls"`, XZ | inner and outer: `u`, `w` dirichlet (zero); every other variable neumann (zero gradient) |
| `lateral = "walls"`, cylindrical (the only choice) | inner (axis): `u`, `v` dirichlet; every other variable, `w` included, neumann. outer (wall): `u` dirichlet; every other variable, `v` and `w` included, neumann |
| `lateral = "periodic"` (XZ, single patch only) | inner and outer: periodic on every variable |
| `vertical_scalars = "d2"` | bottom of every variable: second_derivative (zero); then the `w` and sedimentation rules below |
| `vertical_scalars = "natural"` | bottom of every variable: natural (unconstrained); then the rules below |
| `vertical_scalars = "neumann"` | bottom of every variable: neumann; then the rules below |
| `vertical_scalars = "r1t1x"` | bottom as `d2`, except `rho_d`, `rho_t`, `E_t`, `Q_ss` neumann and `p` r1t1x (the rigid-wall pressure condition `dp'/dz = -g rho_t'`, installed before every fit; relaxed on `numerics.wall_bc_tau`) |
| `vertical_scalars_lid = <same values>` | the same rule at the top of every variable (default `natural`; `d2` at the lid drifts warm over days); then the rules below |
| (always) | `w` dirichlet (zero) at bottom and top, whatever `vertical_scalars` and `vertical_scalars_lid` |
| (always) | the sedimenting slots (rain; the rain number under two-moment rain; the twelve ice slots under ISHMAEL) natural at the bottom, so they fall out |
| `sedimentation_lid = "natural"` | the sedimenting slots natural at the top too |
| `sedimentation_lid = "wall"` | the sedimenting slots keep the `vertical_scalars_lid` condition at the top |
| (always, B-spline vertical) | the sedimentation FLUX of every sedimenting slot is fitted with a zero-flux (dirichlet) lid, whatever its slot's own top BC: nothing falls in from above (`[extra.options] sedimentation_flux_lid = "natural"` undoes this, forensics only) |
| nests (not configurable) | at each junction the finer patch's side is r3x (its border value, slope and curvature pinned to the coarser parent at run time) and the coarser patch's side is natural (its free collar termination, one parent cell inside the child) |

`[boundary_conditions.override]` sets single entries after these rules, for experiments:

```toml
[boundary_conditions.override]
nu_r = { top = "dirichlet" }            # or a [boundary_conditions.override.nu_r] table
```

Sides: `inner`, `outer`, `bottom`, `top`. Values: `natural`, `dirichlet`, `neumann`, `second_derivative`, `periodic`, `r1t1x`.
The variable must be one the run has (an error lists them); `inner`/`outer` act on the
domain's own edges (the first patch's inner side, the last patch's outer side), never on a
nest interface, and are refused under `lateral = "periodic"`.

Every run writes the resolved table to `<output.dir>/boundary_conditions.toml` (one
`[[patch]]` per patch, one `[[patch.variable]]` per variable) and prints its compact
form at startup. The tables of the cases here, generated from their `scythe_config.toml`
(a single lateral name = both sides; `p<i>` = patch `i`):

## The `[extra.*]` escape hatch

`[extra.options]` and `[extra.physical_params]` pass keys straight into the model's
`options` / `physical_params` dicts, for the knobs no typed section owns. Every key is
checked against the registries below (a misspelled key is an error, not silently
ignored) and coerced to the registered type; `physical_params` holds numbers only. A key
a typed section produces ("owned by") is refused there, so each setting has exactly one
spelling. `Kvdiff`, `Kvdiff_heat` and `Kvdiff_water` are deliberately not owned: the
build writes them as 0 (vertical mixing belongs to the boundary-layer scheme) and
`[extra.physical_params]` is the way to override them.

```toml
[extra.options]
mynn_edmf_mom = false
[extra.physical_params]
co2_ppm = 280.0
```

### `[extra.options]` keys (`KNOWN_OPTION_KEYS`)

| key | type | owned by | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bl_K_ref` | float | `diagnostics.timestep_advisory.bl_K_ref` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | timestep advisory: reference BL eddy diffusivity [m^2/s] (reference_state.jl) |
| `cfl_interval` | float | `numerics.cfl_interval` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | CFL report cadence [s]; default output_interval (semiimplicit.jl, nesting.jl) |
| `clamp_water` | bool |  | floor negative untransformed water at zero after each step (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `column_state_guard` | bool |  | located error when p, rho_d, rho_t or T is not positive/finite after the retrieval; default true, false is forensics only (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `condensate_floor` | string (enum) |  | cloud flooring at the thermodynamic interface: :none or :diagnostic (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `condensate_transform` | string (enum) | `physics.microphysics.condensate_transform` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | cloud-slot control variable: :none, :bhyp, :bhyp_smooth (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `condensation` | bool | `physics.microphysics.condensation` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | phase change on/off: QSS condensation and the ice transfers (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `consistent_qss_reference` | bool | `reference_state.consistent_qss` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | reference Q_ss rebuilt consistently with the discrete retrieval (semiimplicit.jl, moist_compressible.jl) |
| `exact_reference_state` | bool | `reference_state.exact` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | read the pre-balanced exact reference-state file (semiimplicit.jl) |
| `exact_si` | bool | `numerics.exact_si` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | exact coupled semi-implicit acoustic solve, variant 1 (exact_si.jl, moist_compressible.jl) |
| `exact_si_ax0` | bool |  | exact_si axisym: experimental axis-row treatment of the radial operator (exact_si.jl) |
| `exact_si_zero_x` | bool |  | exact_si diagnostic: zero the horizontal increments (exact_si.jl) |
| `horizontal_semiimplicit` | bool | `numerics.horizontal_semiimplicit` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | horizontal semi-implicit acoustic terms, XZ RiRk only (horizontal_si.jl, exact_si.jl) |
| `hsi_cross_comp` | bool |  | horizontal SI factorization cross-term compensation, low-Courant experiments only (horizontal_si.jl) |
| `hsi_scheme` | string |  | horizontal SI weights: "ai2s" or "am2" (horizontal_si.jl) |
| `hsi_u_history` | string |  | horizontal SI u history: "none" or "stored" (horizontal_si.jl) |
| `hsi_x_history` | string |  | horizontal SI x history: "fresh" or lagged (horizontal_si.jl, moist_compressible.jl) |
| `hydrostatic_reference` | bool | `reference_state.hydrostatic` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | discretely hydrostatic reference state (semiimplicit.jl) |
| `ice_agg_caps` | bool |  | ISHMAEL aggregation caps on the unit pass (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_anchor_floor` | bool |  | ice anchor reconciliation: floor leg (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_anchor_flux` | bool |  | ice anchor reconciliation: flux leg (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_anchor_rates` | bool |  | ice anchor reconciliation: rates leg (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_anchor_source` | bool |  | ice anchor removal source (the census is kept when off) (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_attr_census` | bool |  | ice attribution census in the log (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_microphysics` | string (enum) | `physics.microphysics.ice` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | ice scheme: :ishmael or :none (moist_compressible.jl, radiation_state.jl, mc_mynn_bl.jl) |
| `ice_number_realization` | bool |  | per-donor realization bound on the ice-number sinks (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_population_seed` | string (enum) |  | crystal seeding of number-less ice below T_0: :local or :large (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_population_source` | bool |  | ice population source for number-less ice (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_shed_above_t0` | bool |  | shed riming to rain above T_0 (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_transform` | string (enum) | `physics.microphysics.ice_transform` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | control variable of the twelve ice slots: :none, :bhyp, :bhyp_smooth (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `ice_var_check` | bool |  | ISHMAEL var_check write-back as a relaxation source (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `lobe_relaxation` | bool |  | relax a transformed water-mass slot's (cloud, rain, the three ice masses) refit lobe nu < 0 toward 0 on physical_params[:tau_lobe] where that species' channel is closed (recovered density 0, every process term of the slot exactly 0); moves no recovered mass, water-neutral while rho_t is prognostic; a pragmatic device, not physics (Stage L, reference/RHO_T_RETIREMENT_DESIGN.md); refused with water_lobe_attribution (moist_compressible.jl) |
| `louis_bl` | bool | `physics.boundary_layer.scheme` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | Louis first-order vertical mixing (moist_compressible.jl, mc_surface_layer.jl) |

| `mynn_check_values` | bool |  | MYNN finite-value checks every call (mynn_state.jl) |
| `mynn_closure` | float |  | MYNN closure level; only 2.5 is ported (mynn_state.jl) |
| `mynn_edmf` | int | `physics.boundary_layer.mynn_edmf` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | MYNN mass flux: 0 off, 1 on (mynn_state.jl) |
| `mynn_edmf_mom` | bool |  | EDMF momentum transport (mynn_state.jl) |
| `mynn_fidelity` | Union{Symbol, Vector{Symbol}} | `physics.boundary_layer.mynn_fidelity` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | MYNN closure fidelity: :scythe, :fortran or a Vector of deviations (mynn_state.jl) |
| `mynn_init` | string (enum) | `physics.boundary_layer.mynn_init` (refused in `[extra.options]`) | MYNN TKE initialisation: :taper or :zero (mynn_state.jl) |
